original_question: Suppose q_1, ..., q_m : F2^n -> F2 are degree-at-most-2 polynomials and the indicator of the all-ones vector, namely AND : F2^n -> {-1,1}, can be written as AND(x) = sum_{i=1}^m c_i (-1)^{q_i(x)} for real coefficients c_i. What lower bound on m is necessary?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the unnumbered open problem titled "Uncertainty Principle for Quadratic Fourier Analysis" in O'Donnell's list of open problems. ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures almost all of the paper's official formulation: the ambient domain is \(\mathbb{F}_2^n\), the functions \(q_1,\dots,q_m\) are \(\mathbb{F}_2\)-polynomials of degree at most 2, the representation is exact of the form \(\mathrm{AND}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i(-1)^{q_i(x)}\), the coefficients are real, and the question asks for a necessary lower bound on the number of quadratic phases \(m\). ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's phrase "indicator function of \((1,\dots,1)\)" should be made explicit in stand-alone form: \(\mathrm{AND}(1,\dots,1)=1\) and \(\mathrm{AND}(x)=-1\) for every other \(x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n\). ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))

It should say that the identity is required pointwise for all \(x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n\), not approximately and not merely in correlation. ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))

The quantifier over \(n\) is implicit in the paper's wording; to be fully stand-alone, the question should ask for a lower bound on the minimum possible \(m\) as a function of \(n\). ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))

The paper imposes no extra restrictions such as homogeneity, distinctness of the \(q_i\), or any side condition beyond degree at most 2; making that explicit prevents accidental broadening or narrowing. ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))

Because the paper's front page defers notation and definitions to an external source, a self-contained rewrite should spell out the codomains and sign convention explicitly rather than assuming the reader knows the paper's Boolean-function conventions. ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))
refined_question: For each positive integer \(n\), let \(\mathrm{AND}:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\{-1,1\}\) be the \{-1,1\}-valued indicator of the point \((1,\dots,1)\), i.e. \(\mathrm{AND}(1,\dots,1)=1\) and \(\mathrm{AND}(x)=-1\) for all \(x\neq(1,\dots,1)\). Suppose there exist polynomials \(q_1,\dots,q_m:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2\) of degree at most 2 and real coefficients \(c_1,\dots,c_m\) such that, for every \(x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n\), \(\mathrm{AND}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i(-1)^{q_i(x)}\). What lower bound, as a function of \(n\), must hold on the minimum possible number \(m\) of quadratic phase terms in such an exact representation?
justification: This is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of the paper's own problem statement, so the faithful target is the problem itself rather than a neighboring broader question. The nearby remarks also fix the intended scale of the question: Hatami can show \(m\ge n\), conjectures that \(m\ge 2^{\Omega(n)}\) is necessary, and notes that in the degree-1 case the exact answer is \(m=2^n\). That context shows the paper is asking for asymptotic lower bounds on exact quadratic-phase representations of the \{-1,1\}-valued AND/point-mass function, not about approximation, correlation, or a broader constant-degree framework. ([cs.cmu.edu](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/aobf-open-problems.pdf))
